# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]

I see a green light, display reading 9, and five wires in order: white, green, red, yellow, purple. The gestures received from the others have no established meaning yet, so I will relay the bomb’s visible information to both teammates.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 9. The light is green. Wires from 1 to 5 are white, green, red, yellow, purple.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 9. The light is green. Wires from 1 to 5 are white, green, red, yellow, purple.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display 9, green light, and wires white, green, red, yellow, purple. Mute made 👌, but no meaning has been established for that gesture, so I cannot safely infer anything from it. I should remind Mute to communicate the manual’s instructions directly to Blind by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The display, light, and wires are unchanged. I cannot interpret 👌 safely. Please tell Blind the manual instructions by speech.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 9, green light, and wires 1–5 are white, green, red, yellow, and purple. Mute has sent 🤟, but that sign has no agreed meaning, so I cannot use it as an instruction. I will again provide Blind the complete visible state and ask Mute to convey the manual’s actual procedure aloud.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb state is unchanged: display 9, green light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind; gestures have no established meaning.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb state is still unchanged. Mute’s three ☝ gestures have no agreed meaning, so I will establish an unambiguous code rather than guess. Mute can hear this message and then return the manual’s instruction as Morse using gestures; Blind should wait for the decoded instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="We have no agreed meaning for ☝. Please encode the manual's complete required action in International Morse: use 👍 for dot, 👎 for dash, 👌 between letters, and 🤟 at the end. Send it over as gesture sequences, one sequence per turn if needed.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch or alter anything yet. I am obtaining the manual's exact instruction from Mute using a gesture code.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 🤟]

Mute’s Morse message decodes as `WIRE3`: `.--` = W, `..` = I, `.-.` = R, `.` = E, and `...--` = 3. I will tell Blind to act on wire 3, which I see is the red wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's manual instruction decodes to WIRE3. Act on wire 3, the red wire.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 3 was correct and the bomb has changed. I now see display 4, a yellow light, wire 3 cut, and wires 1, 2, 4, and 5 still white, green, yellow, and purple respectively. I will report this new state so Mute can consult the next manual step and Blind can wait for it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct wire cut. New state: display 4, yellow light; wire 3 is cut; wire 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Please provide the next manual instruction to Blind using our Morse gesture code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Correct wire 3 cut. New state: display 4, yellow light; wire 3 is cut; wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Await Mute's next manual instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🤟]

Mute’s Morse message decodes to `WIRE5`: `.--` = W, `..` = I, `.-.` = R, `.` = E, and `.....` = 5. I will tell Blind to cut wire 5, which I see is purple.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's manual instruction decodes to WIRE5. Cut wire 5, the purple wire.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms wire 5 was also correct. The bomb now shows display 3 and a green light; wires 3 and 5 are cut, while wires 1, 2, and 4 remain white, green, and yellow. The repeated gesture sequence still decodes to WIRE5, which has already been correctly cut, so it is not a new instruction. I will request the next manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 3, green light; wires 3 and 5 cut; wire 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow. The repeated message was WIRE5, already completed. Please send the next manual instruction using the Morse gesture code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 3, green light; wires 3 and 5 cut; wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow. Await the next manual instruction.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤟]

Mute’s Morse message decodes to `WIRE1`: `.--` = W, `..` = I, `.-.` = R, `.` = E, and `.----` = 1. I will instruct Blind to cut wire 1, the white wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's manual instruction decodes to WIRE1. Cut wire 1, the white wire.")
```
